exact_identity_review.carrier_and_law: Finite-dimensional real inner-product E, μ=stdGaussian E with covariance identity. X,Y are independent under μ×μ. Arbitrary centered IsGaussian covariance would need its covariance operator in Stein/concentration; this route may not silently generalize the numerical L² coefficient to arbitrary Gaussian μ.
exact_identity_review.rotation: Uθ=cosθ X+sinθ Y, Vθ=−sinθ X+cosθ Y. Uθ′=Vθ. Inverse X=cosθ Uθ−sinθ Vθ. Pinned ContinuousLinearMap.rotation has exactly this orientation, not opposite-angle convention. μ×μ rotation-invariance plus mean-zero stdGaussian gives U,V independent standardGaussians.
exact_identity_review.Stein: For globally C¹ Lipschitz h and deterministic v∈E: ∫⟨v,x⟩h(x)dμ=∫Dh(x)[v]dμ. Write φ(x)=(2π)^(−d/2)exp(−‖x‖²/2), Dφ(x)[v]=−⟨x,v⟩φ(x); Haar full-space IBP gives the positive Stein sign.
exact_identity_review.F_derivative: F(θ)=E[f(X)g(Uθ)]. C¹ g and product domination justify F′(θ)=E[f(X)⟨∇g(Uθ),Vθ⟩]. Re-express in independent U,V before applying V-Stein to h_U(v)=f(cosθ U−sinθ v) with direction∇g(U), deterministic after fixingU. Then D_v h_U[∇g(U)]=−sinθ⟨∇f(X),∇g(U)⟩. Thus F′=−sinθ E⟨∇f(X),∇g(Uθ)⟩. No derivative/Hessian ofg is required by V-Stein.
exact_identity_review.endpoints: F(0)=E[f g]; F(π/2)=(Ef)(Eg). FTC gives Cov(f,g)=F(0)−F(π/2)=∫_0^(π/2)sinθ E⟨∇f(X),∇g(Uθ)⟩dθ. ∫sinθ=1, with no missing cosine/2/π factor.
exact_identity_review.Herbst: Let m=Ef, M(t)=E exp(t(f−m)), g_t=exp(t(f−m)). For t≥0, ∇g_t=t g_t∇f and ‖∇f‖≤L. Cov(f,g_t)=M′(t)≤t L²∫_0^(π/2)sinθ E[g_t(Uθ)]dθ=t L²M(t). M(0)=1 and M(t)>0; integrate (logM)′≤tL² to obtain logM(t)≤t²L²/2. For t<0 apply the positive result to−f, using genuine E(−f)=−m. Exact1/2 is correct.
exact_identity_review.C1_suffices: C¹ globally Lipschitz f gives continuous bounded gradient, enough for Stein and covariance. g_t is C¹ but generally NOT globally Lipschitz; its gradient has controlled exponential growth. Route is sound because Stein is applied only to h_U, never to g_t as a globally Lipschitz function. A generic covariance lemma restricted to globally Lipschitzg cannot be used directly for g_t without a separately justified extension.
